kind: §6.N bluff-hunt — KOTLIN / client side (parallel fleet cycle)
protocol: Seventh Law clause 5 + §6.N.2 production-code coverage — pick gate-shaping Kotlin production files; mutation-rehearse to prove existing tests bite on real, NON-crashing, user-visible breakage. REAL observed-failure evidence captured verbatim from JUnit XML reports.
scope: Kotlin / Android client. Sibling Go-side hunts this cycle covered auth middleware + providers handler + parsers; the sibling Kotlin hunt (2026-06-13-kotlin-dynamic-provider-consumer.json) covered RemoteTrackerDescriptor.from() capability mapping + the DTO encoding bridge. This hunt covers the TWO DISTINCT gate-shaping production functions those did not touch: the auth-key attachment in ProviderCatalogRepository.fetchProviders, and the replace-vs-merge logic in DefaultTrackerRegistry.populateFrom.
tooling: GOMAXPROCS=2 ./gradlew :<module>:testDebugUnitTest --tests <FQTN> --max-workers=2 --console=plain (per-module, not the tree; a distribute was running — §6.T.2 resource limits).
host_note: Worktree submodules were uninitialized; tracker_sdk (the only includeBuild dependency for these modules) was checked out from the shared .git/modules store at the parent's pin 7afc37aaa6 so the JVM build could resolve :tracker_sdk:api. No host-direct emulators, no live ADB devices, no network egress to real trackers — pure JVM MockWebServer unit tests.
selection_filter: Both files just became load-bearing for the dynamic-provider onboarding flow (2026-06-11/06-12 Defect-A + Defect-B). Filter 'would a bug here be invisible to existing tests?' — the catalogue fetch's auth-key wiring and the registry's replace-not-merge semantics are exactly the two production decisions whose silent regression produced the real-device 'only 4 providers' / 'wrong provider set' symptoms.

targets.production_under_test: lava.data.provider.ProviderCatalogRepository.fetchProviders(apiBaseUrl, authKey) — the Defect-A fix: when authKey != null, derive a per-call client that attaches the Lava-Auth header (withAuthKey) so the on-device api-app's auth gate admits the GET /providers request; without it the gate 401s and onboarding falls back to the 4 bundled providers.
targets.mutation_applied: In fetchProviders, replaced `val client = if (authKey != null) lanHttpClient.withAuthKey(authKey, authFieldName) else lanHttpClient` with `val client = lanHttpClient` — i.e. NEVER attach the auth key; every fetch goes out unauthenticated (the pre-Defect-A wiring class).
targets.test_outcome_after_mutation: fail (CLEAN) — BUILD FAILED, 6 tests completed, 1 failed
targets.test_failure_message_verbatim: java.lang.AssertionError: expected success, was: Failure(java.lang.IllegalStateException: provider discovery failed: HTTP 401 for https://localhost:50692/providers)  [ProviderCatalogRepositoryTest.kt:159, test fetchOverSelfSignedTlsWithAuthSucceeds]
targets.user_visible_break_caught: The auth-gated MockWebServer dispatcher 401s the keyless request; the parsed-catalogue success assertion (incl. the API-only Jackett '1337x' provider that proves >4 providers) cannot be reached → the exact 'only 4 providers in onboarding' symptom (Crashlytics 042b9b61).
targets.remediation: N/A — fetchOverSelfSignedTlsWithAuthSucceeds asserts on result.isSuccess + the parsed descriptors + (secondarily) the on-the-wire Lava-Auth header (server.takeRequest().getHeader). Primary assertion is on the user-visible provider list. Falsifiable on exactly the auth-key branch the test claims to cover. The dedicated discrimination tests strictClientFailsTheHandshake (TLS boundary) and missingAuthKeyIsRejectedByTheGate (gate boundary) remain green and codify the pre-fix behaviours.
targets.reverted: yes — git checkout, ProviderCatalogRepository.kt matches HEAD byte-for-byte (git diff --quiet clean).

targets.production_under_test: lava.tracker.registry.DefaultTrackerRegistry.populateFrom(descriptors) — the spec §4.2 runtime-source-of-truth REPLACE semantics: a non-empty API catalogue REPLACES the bundled set (every bundled id NOT re-declared by the catalogue is unregistered), so a provider the chosen API does not offer is removed from the list the user sees. Exercised end-to-end through the REAL OnboardingViewModel.fetchAndPopulateProviders → REAL FetchProvidersUseCase → REAL ProviderCatalogRepository over MockWebServer (only the TCP-probe + socket boundaries faked, §6.J Second Law).
targets.mutation_applied: In populateFrom, commented out the bundled-eviction loop (`bundledFactories.keys.forEach { bundledId -> if (bundledId !in incomingIds) delegate.unregister(bundledId) }`) — i.e. MERGE instead of REPLACE: bundled providers the API does not offer survive alongside the API set.
targets.test_outcome_after_mutation: fail (CLEAN) — BUILD FAILED, 3 tests completed, 1 failed
targets.test_failure_message_verbatim: java.lang.AssertionError: bundled 'rutracker' (NOT in the chosen API's catalogue) MUST be ABSENT — the list comes FROM the API, not merged with bundled. was [rutracker, yts, thepiratebay]  [test: onboarding shows ONLY the chosen API's providers replacing bundled ones the API lacks]
targets.user_visible_break_caught: With merge, the chosen API supports {thepiratebay, yts} but the user is also shown the bundled 'rutracker' the API does NOT support — the operator's literal requirement ('all listed providers MUST be obtained from the API because some APIs may or may not support all providers') is violated. Test catches it as a non-crashing user-visible list-content break.
targets.remediation: N/A — the test drives the real ViewModel→UseCase→Repository→registry stack and its PRIMARY assertions are on state.providers (the rendered list set equals the API set; the bundled-only id is absent) — user-visible state per Sixth Law clause 3. The same mutation is independently guarded one layer down by core/tracker/registry DynamicRegistryTest; this hunt confirms the CONSUMER-level (onboarding) test bites too.
targets.reverted: yes — git checkout, DefaultTrackerRegistry.kt matches HEAD byte-for-byte (git diff --quiet clean).
